mainTopic: Agents as witnesses to their own act (רב נחמן, and how the money case works), then who may accept a נערה's גט and קידושין: her, her father, or both.
overview: This amud opens with the end of רב נחמן's rule: the שלוחים who carried out an act can also testify about it. That is true for קידושין and גירושין, and the same is true in דיני ממונות. The גמרא explains why all three cases had to be taught, since each has its own reason to suspect the agents might lie. It then asks how the money case works. If a loan made before witnesses had to be repaid before witnesses, the agents would gain from their own testimony. So רב נחמן must hold that repayment needs no witnesses, and a מיגו makes the agents believable. Now that the חכמים set up שבועת היסת, the agents and the lender each swear, and the borrower pays again. The גמרא then turns to the line "a man can betroth his daughter." It quotes a משנה in גיטין about who may receive a נערה's גט. ריש לקיש says the same argument applies to קידושין. רבי יוחנן says that for קידושין only the father accepts, and רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא explains why: a גט brings her back into her father's authority, while קידושין take her out of it. The amud ends as the גמרא begins a challenge from the case of מאמר, and the source it quotes appears on the next amud.

steps.title: The same rule applies to money cases
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן ends his rule: just as שלוחים can testify about the קידושין or גירושין they carried out, they can also testify in דיני ממונות.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the same is true in money cases.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the last line of רב נחמן's rule. Agents sent for a money matter, like paying back a debt, may testify that they did it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב נחמן already allowed שלוחים to testify for קידושין and גירושין. Now he adds a third area, money. This gives three parallel cases, which sets up the גמרא's next question: why did he need to list all three?

keyTerms.meaning: Money cases; monetary law
And likewise; and the same is true

phrases.english: And the same is true in money cases.
phrases.notes: This finishes רב נחמן's rule that the agents who did the act can be its witnesses. Here, think of agents sent to pay off someone's debt.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes רב נחמן's statement from just before this point (קידושין and גירושין) by adding a third case.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: שלוחים who carried out a money matter, such as repaying a debt, may testify that they did it.

steps.title: Why divorce cannot be learned from betrothal
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins explaining why all three cases are needed. From קידושין alone, we could not learn גירושין, because in גירושין there is a new worry that the agent wants to marry the woman himself.
steps.simpleTranslation: And it is necessary to teach all of them. If he had taught us only betrothal, we would say they are believed because they come to make her forbidden. But in divorce, we should worry that maybe the agent has his eye on her.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is answering an unspoken question: why list three cases when one would seem enough? It starts with why קידושין does not teach us גירושין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In קידושין, the agents' testimony makes the woman forbidden to everyone, including themselves, so they have nothing to gain by lying. In גירושין, their testimony makes her free to remarry, so an agent who wants her might lie to free her. That is why רב נחמן had to say clearly that גירושין works too.

keyTerms.meaning: It is necessary, meaning each case teaches something the others could not
He taught us; he let us hear
To make her forbidden to other men
We should worry; we should suspect
He set his eyes on her; he wants to marry her

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the גמרא is saying the agents in גירושין are not believed. It is only showing that without רב נחמן saying so, we would have worried. His rule tells us they are believed.

phrases.english: And it is necessary, for if he had taught us only betrothal,
that is because they come to make her forbidden,
but divorce,
we should worry that maybe he has set his eyes on her.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains why רב נחמן needed to list several cases, starting with קידושין versus גירושין.
steps.terutzResolutionType: צריכותא: each case has its own reason to suspect the agents, so each must be taught.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Agents are believed in קידושין only because they gain nothing; in גירושין we would suspect one of them wants to marry her.
steps.terutzMaskana: רב נחמן taught גירושין on its own to show that agents are believed there too.

steps.title: Why money cannot be learned from divorce
steps.stepSummary: From גירושין alone we could not learn money cases, because a woman cannot marry two men, but two agents could split money between them. So all three cases are needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if he had taught us only divorce, we would say they are believed because a woman cannot be fit for two men. But in money cases, I might say these two would split it. Therefore all the cases are necessary.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the צריכותא. It shows that money is different from גירושין, and concludes that all three cases are needed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In גירושין there are two agents, and one woman cannot marry both of them, so it is unlikely that both would lie for her. Money can easily be divided, so both agents could plot to keep the debt money and falsely say they paid. Since each case has its own worry, רב נחמן had to teach all of them.

keyTerms.meaning: A woman
She is not fit for two men at once
They would surely split it
They are all necessary

steps.whatToRemember: Three cases, three worries: קידושין has no reason to lie, in גירושין one agent might want her, and in money both agents could share the money. רב נחמן's rule covers all three.

phrases.english: And if he had taught us only divorce,

phrases.aramaic: מִשּׁוּם דְּאִיתְּתָא לְבֵי תְרֵי לָא חַזְיָא,
phrases.english: that is because a woman is not fit for two men,
phrases.notes: Only one of the two agents could marry her, so it is unlikely that both would lie together for her.

phrases.english: but with money, I might say:
these two would split it.
So all of them are necessary.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the צריכותא by comparing גירושין with money, then concludes that all three cases are needed.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Each of רב נחמן's three cases is needed, because each has its own possible reason for the agents to lie.

steps.title: If debts must be repaid before witnesses, the agents benefit from their testimony
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what רב נחמן holds about repaying a loan. If he holds that a loan given in front of witnesses must be repaid in front of witnesses, then the agents gain from saying they paid, so they should not be allowed to testify.
steps.simpleTranslation: What does he hold? If he holds that one who lends to his friend in front of witnesses must be repaid in front of witnesses, then these agents are affected by their own testimony. For if they say 'We did not pay him,' the sender will say to them: 'Then pay me back!'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is now testing the money case. It asks which view on repaying loans רב נחמן holds, and shows that the first option creates a problem.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If repayment needs witnesses, the agents cannot simply say 'we gave the money back to you,' because they have no witnesses for that either. So if they admit they did not pay the lender, the sender can demand his money from them. That gives them a reason to falsely say they paid, which makes them נוגעים בעדות, and witnesses who gain from their testimony are not accepted.

keyTerms.meaning: What does he hold?
One who lends to another in front of witnesses
To repay him
Witnesses who have a personal stake in their testimony, and so are not accepted
Pay me back

steps.confusionAlert: The money that the sender asks for here is not the lender's money. It is the sender's own money, which he handed the agents to pay the debt. If they say they did not pay the lender, the sender wants it back from them.
steps.whyThisMatters: This question challenges whether רב נחמן's money case can work at all. The answer depends on the rule about repaying a loan in front of witnesses, and the גמרא will keep exploring this next.

phrases.english: What does he hold?
If he holds that one who lends to his friend in front of witnesses
must be repaid in front of witnesses,
then these agents have a personal stake in their testimony,
for if they say: 'We did not pay him,'
he will say to them: 'Then pay me back!'
phrases.notes: 'He' is the man who sent them. He wants back the money he gave them to pay off his debt.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי קָסָבַר? אִי קָסָבַר הַמַּלְוֶה חֲבֵירוֹ בְּעֵדִים צָרִיךְ לְפוֹרְעוֹ בְּעֵדִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After showing all three cases are needed, the גמרא examines how the money case could work, and raises a problem with the first possible view.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב נחמן's ruling that שלוחים can testify that they repaid a debt (step 1).
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If repayment requires witnesses, agents who admit they did not pay would owe the sender his money, since they cannot prove they returned it. That stake makes them נוגעים בעדות, so they should not be believed as witnesses.

steps.title: רב נחמן holds a loan need not be repaid in front of witnesses
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן holds that a loan made in front of witnesses does not need to be repaid in front of witnesses. The agents could have said they gave the money back to the borrower, so they are believed when they say they paid the lender.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רב נחמן really holds that someone who lends money in front of witnesses does not need to be repaid in front of witnesses. Since the agents could have said, "We gave the money back to the borrower," they can also say, "We paid the lender."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from step 4 by choosing the other option. רב נחמן holds that repayment does not need witnesses.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question in step 4 was that the agents gain something by saying they paid. But if repayment needs no witnesses, the agents could have gotten out of trouble just as easily by saying they returned the money to the borrower. Since that easier claim was open to them, they gain nothing by saying they paid the lender. So they are believed (this kind of reasoning is called a מיגו).

keyTerms.meaning: The lender
The borrower
To repay him
Since (he could have made a better claim, we believe this one)

steps.confusionAlert: The agents here are not ordinary witnesses. They are the people who were sent with the money. The whole question is whether they have a personal interest in what they say.

phrases.english: Rather, he actually holds:
phrases.notes: "He" is רב נחמן. The גמרא is now taking the second side of its question from step 4.

phrases.english: one who lends to his fellow in front of witnesses
does not need to be repaid in front of witnesses,
and since they (the agents) could say:
"We returned it to the borrower,"
they can say: "We paid the lender."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 4 by choosing the second option.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Picks the other side of the question: repayment does not need witnesses.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: If רב נחמן held that repayment needs witnesses, the agents would gain from their testimony.
steps.terutzMaskana: Repayment needs no witnesses, so a מיגו makes the agents believable.

steps.title: Since שבועת היסת was set up, both sides swear and the borrower pays again
steps.stepSummary: Now that the חכמים have set up שבועת היסת, the agents swear that they gave the money, the lender swears that he did not get it, and the borrower pays the lender again.
steps.simpleTranslation: And now that the חכמים set up the oath of היסת, these witnesses swear, "We gave it to him." The lender swears that he did not take it. Then the borrower pays the lender.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a later update: in its own time, the ruling of רב נחמן no longer works the same way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once שבועת היסת exists, an agent who says "we returned it to the borrower" would have to swear. So that claim is no longer an easy way out, and the מיגו from step 5 is gone. The agents can no longer free the borrower. Instead, each side swears, and the borrower ends up paying the lender a second time.

keyTerms.meaning: An oath the חכמים require from someone who completely denies a claim
The חכמים set up (a rule)
They swear

steps.whatToRemember: In the time of רב נחמן, the agents were believed because of a מיגו. After שבועת היסת was set up, the agents and the lender both swear, and the borrower pays again.

phrases.english: And now that the Rabbis have instituted
the oath of היסת –
these witnesses swear
phrases.notes: "These witnesses" are the agents who were sent with the money.

phrases.english: that "we gave it to him,"
and the lender swears that he did not take it,
and the borrower pays the lender.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Updates the ruling of step 5 to fit the later rule of שבועת היסת.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Today the agents and the lender each swear, and the borrower pays the lender again.

steps.title: A משנה in גיטין about who receives a נערה's גט
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא turns to our משנה's line "A man can betroth his daughter." It quotes a משנה in גיטין: the תנא קמא says both the נערה and her father can receive her גט, while רבי יהודה says only her father can.
steps.simpleTranslation: "A man can betroth his daughter." We learned in a משנה there: a betrothed נערה, she and her father can both receive her גט. רבי יהודה said: two hands cannot acquire as one; rather, her father receives her גט. And any girl who cannot guard her גט cannot be divorced.
steps.whatsHappening: This opens a new topic. The גמרא quotes a משנה about divorce to set up a question about קידושין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תנא קמא allows either the girl or her father to receive the גט. רבי יהודה says two people cannot both have the power to acquire for her, so only the father can. The משנה adds that a girl too young to guard her גט cannot be divorced at all.

keyTerms.meaning: A betrothed young woman (roughly ages 12 to 12½)
Her bill of divorce
Two hands acquiring as one (two people both having the power to acquire for the same person)
We learned in a משנה elsewhere

phrases.english: "A man can betroth his daughter."
phrases.notes: These words are quoted from our משנה. They show which line we are now discussing.

phrases.english: We learned there:
A betrothed young woman –
she and her father can receive her bill of divorce.
Rabbi Yehuda said:
Two hands do not acquire as one,
rather, her father receives her bill of divorce.

phrases.aramaic: וְכֹל שֶׁאֵין יְכוֹלָה לִשְׁמוֹר אֶת גִּיטָּהּ –
phrases.english: And any girl who is unable to guard her bill of divorce –
cannot be divorced.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָאִישׁ מְקַדֵּשׁ אֶת בִּתּוֹ. תְּנַן הָתָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new section on a different line of our משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The תנא קמא says the נערה or her father can receive her גט. רבי יהודה says only her father can.

steps.title: ריש לקיש: the same argument applies to קידושין
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש says the argument about receiving a גט also applies to receiving קידושין.
steps.simpleTranslation: ריש לקיש said: just as there is an argument about divorce, so too there is an argument about betrothal.
steps.whatsHappening: ריש לקיש takes the argument from the משנה in גיטין and applies it to קידושין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to ריש לקיש, the תנא קמא would also let the נערה accept her own קידושין, while רבי יהודה would say only her father can. Divorce and betrothal follow the same rule.

keyTerms.meaning: A disagreement
Divorce

phrases.english: Reish Lakish said:
Just as there is a dispute regarding divorce,
so too there is a dispute regarding betrothal.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the argument in the משנה from step 7 to קידושין.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The disagreement between the תנא קמא and רבי יהודה applies to קידושין as well.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: for קידושין everyone agrees only the father accepts
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says the argument is only about divorce. For קידושין, everyone agrees that her father accepts them and she does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יוחנן said: the argument is about divorce, but about betrothal everyone agrees that her father accepts it, and not she.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן disagrees with ריש לקיש and limits the argument to divorce only.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רבי יוחנן, even the תנא קמא, who lets the girl receive her own גט, agrees that only the father can accept her קידושין. So divorce and betrothal are treated differently.

keyTerms.meaning: Everyone agrees
Her father, and not she

steps.whatToRemember: ריש לקיש: the argument applies to both גט and קידושין. רבי יוחנן: it applies only to a גט; for קידושין, only the father accepts.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yochanan said:
The dispute is regarding divorce,
but regarding betrothal –
everyone agrees: her father, and not she.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אָמַר: מַחְלוֹקֶת לְגֵירוּשִׁין, אֲבָל לְקִידּוּשִׁין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposite view to ריש לקיש in step 8.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: For קידושין, everyone agrees that only the father can accept them for a נערה.

steps.title: The reason behind רבי יוחנן's split between divorce and betrothal
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא explains the logic. A גט returns her to her father's authority, so she or her father can receive it. קידושין remove her from his authority, so only he can accept them.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא said: What is רבי יוחנן's reason, according to the רבנן? With divorce, she is bringing herself back into her father's authority, so either she or her father can receive the גט. With betrothal, she is taking herself out of her father's authority, so only her father can accept it, and not she.
steps.whatsHappening: In step 9, רבי יוחנן said that for קידושין everyone agrees only the father accepts them. Here a later אמורא explains the logic behind that difference.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The key question is which direction she is moving. Divorce moves her back toward her father, so letting her receive the גט does not hurt his authority. Betrothal moves her away from her father, so she cannot accept it on her own and only he can.

keyTerms.meaning: According to the view of the רבנן (here, the תנא קמא of the משנה in גיטין)
Her father's authority or control
She brings herself in (back into her father's authority)
She removes herself (out of her father's authority)

steps.whatToRemember: Divorce brings her back to her father, so she or her father can receive the גט. Betrothal takes her away from her father, so only he can accept it.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up a general rule: a נערה cannot do an act that takes her out of her father's authority. The גמרא will now test this rule against another case.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yosei, son of Rabbi Chanina, said:
What is the reason of Rabbi Yochanan
according to the Rabbis?
phrases.notes: The Rabbis here are the תנא קמא from step 7, who said both the girl and her father can receive her גט.

phrases.english: Divorce, where she brings herself into her father's authority:
either she or her father may receive it.
Betrothal, where she removes herself from her father's authority:
her father may accept it, and not she.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי טַעְמֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אַלִּיבָּא דְּרַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reason for רבי יוחנן's statement in step 9
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An act that brings the נערה back into her father's authority (a גט) can be received by her or her father. An act that takes her out of his authority (קידושין) can be accepted only by her father.

steps.title: A challenge from the case of מאמר begins
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא points to מאמר, which also takes her out of her father's authority. It starts to quote a source that seems to disagree with step 10's rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: But there is the case of מאמר, which also takes her out of her father's authority, and we learned:
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a challenge to step 10. It names the case of מאמר and opens a quote with 'ותנן'. The actual source comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 10 said a נערה cannot accept anything that takes her out of her father's authority. מאמר does exactly that, so if a source lets her accept it herself, the reason in step 10 is in trouble. The challenge is only being set up here and is not yet complete.

keyTerms.meaning: A betrothal-like act a יבם does to his יבמה (with money or a document) before יבום
A widow whose husband died without children, waiting for יבום
"And we learned": introduces a quoted תנאי source

steps.confusionAlert: The step ends with 'ותנן:', so the source being quoted has not appeared yet. Do not treat the challenge as finished here.

phrases.english: But there is the case of levirate betrothal,
phrases.notes: מאמר is when a יבם gives his יבמה money or a document as a kind of betrothal, before the actual יבום.

phrases.english: where she removes herself from her father's authority,
and we learned:

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reason given in step 10
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא's reason that a נערה cannot accept an act that takes her out of her father's authority
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: מאמר also takes her out of her father's authority, yet a source (quoted next) seems to treat it differently. This would break the logic of step 10.
